messages.subject: si option
parts:
Hi!
I am running some old code with formula:
f(time,model="rw1",hyper = list(prec = list(param = c(.001, .001))),constr=FALSE,si=FALSE)

but now it marks an error because the si option is not longer on the version I have. I don't even remember what si was for. Is there a substitute?

Thank you,
~Julia

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] si option

On Mon, 2014-10-13 at 16:58 -0400, Julia Palacios wrote:
> Thank you so much Håvard! Do you remember what was this for? I just
> want to make sure I am not missing something important.

si=FALSE is default and does not do anything. si=TRUE, used to say that
some internal computations was stored so that we could compute
simultanous confidence bands for a spline, say. Allthough we could do
that, it was never any big success and we removed it as it was not
properly coded (just a proof of concept code)....

you do not loose anything ;-)))
